title: The Clam That Lives in a Sea Urchin's Throat
description: Off southern Australia, scientists found a new clam species living inside a sea urchin's throat. The host urchin is so fragile it came up only in fragments, but DNA from one throat tube closely matched an urchin species - and inside it were six little clams. Vaticinaria gulicola grows up to 19 millimeters long and lives four to five thousand meters down. It probably traps food particles from the water current the urchin creates; how the clams find and settle into their urchins is still unknown.

title: This Porcupine Glows Blue-Green Under UV Light
description: Biologists in Mexico examined 20 live dwarf porcupines with a UV flashlight - every single one glowed. Blue-green quills, yellow palms and soles. The porcupine isn't making its own light: its quills and skin likely absorb the UV and give it back as visible color. Why they glow is still unknown, but it could help researchers find and study these nocturnal tree-climbers in the wild. Storyboard by @Risala.Toons This video uses an AI-generated voice. Source: Perez-Flores et al., Neotropical Biology
